title: Supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning: an overview

videos.script: The last four lessons of this course are about machine learning, and they are an overview, not a training. {{overview}} Machine learning is a way of writing a program by showing it examples instead of writing its rules. {{definition}} It comes in three kinds, and you have already met two of them in this course. {{met}} When Panela's clusters were found in lesson 15, nobody told the algorithm what a good customer was. That is unsupervised learning. It finds structure. {{unsupervised}} When a model learns from last year's customers which ones stopped ordering, and then predicts it for this year's, that is supervised learning. It learns an answer from examples where the answer is known. {{supervised}} The third kind learns by acting. It tries something, sees the reward, and tries again. An A/B test that sends more visitors to the page that is winning while it is still running is the simplest version of it. {{reinforcement}} This lesson places the three, shows the one danger all of them share, and runs that last idea on Panela's checkout. {{end}}
